answers.answer: For two Spirits, put 8 Fear markers in the pool (4 per Spirit). Use 9 Fear Cards: three, Terror II divider, three, Terror III divider, three. Prepare the Invader deck as 3 Stage I, 4 Stage II, 5 Stage III, with one card of each stage removed unseen; reveal the top card and Explore it as the final setup step, then put it face-up in Build. With a Blight Card, the initial pool is 2 per Spirit plus 1 total (5); without a card, use 5 per Spirit plus 1 total (11).
answers.evidence: Setup: “4 Fear markers per Spirit”; “3 Stage I…4 Stage II…5 Stage III”; “2 Blight per Spirit plus exactly 1 additional Blight total”; introductory pool “5 Blight per Spirit +1 total”; “Initial Explore…last part of setup.”

answers.answer: Yes. Resolve multiple Add Presence placements sequentially, and a newly placed disk may be the origin for the next. Take the leftmost remaining disk from either Presence track for each placement. Energy and Card Plays each use the highest uncovered number on their respective track; numbers are not added together.
answers.evidence: Growth: “With multiple placements, resolve them sequentially: a newly placed disk may be the origin for the next”; take “the leftmost remaining disk from either Presence track.” Tracks: “highest uncovered number”; “Track numbers are not added together.”

answers.answer: With no disks left on tracks, the Add Presence instruction can still be resolved by repositioning one of the Spirit’s existing island Presence. Measure range and select the destination using existing Presence, including the disk being repositioned, then take a disk from anywhere on the island. Destroyed Presence cannot be used unless an effect explicitly permits it.
answers.evidence: Growth: “You may instead reposition any of your island Presence, even with track disks remaining”; “first measure range and select the destination using existing Presence, including the disk about to be repositioned”; “Destroyed Presence cannot be used unless explicitly permitted.”

answers.answer: Pay for all played cards, including Slow cards, during the Spirit Phase; gain their printed Elements immediately when played. Energy from a Fast Power cannot pay those earlier costs. Unspent Energy carries over, but Card Plays cannot be saved for a later turn.
answers.evidence: Play and pay: “paying their printed Energy costs now, including Slow cards” and “Gain every played card’s printed Elements immediately”; “Energy expected from a Fast Power cannot pay these earlier Spirit-phase costs”; unspent Energy carries over; Card Plays “cannot be shared or saved for a later turn.”

answers.answer: A Fast Power cannot be saved for Slow: use it in Fast or forego it. A Power cannot interrupt another Power; finish one before starting another. Select a Slow Power’s target when using it in the Slow Power Phase, based on the then-current board.
answers.evidence: Fast phase: “A Power cannot interrupt another Power”; “A Fast Power cannot be saved for Slow.” Slow phase: “Choose targets now, based on the current board.”

answers.answer: The Invaders deal 3 Damage total (Town 2, Explorer 1) simultaneously to land and Dahan. The land takes 3, so add one Blight. The Dahan take 3: one is destroyed and the other survives with 1 Damage. That surviving Dahan counterattacks for 2 Damage; the players can assign it to destroy the Town, which generates 1 Fear.
answers.evidence: Ravage example states a Town, Explorer and two Dahan cause “3 land Damage (one Blight), and simultaneously 3 Dahan Damage (one dead, one damaged). The survivor can destroy the Town for 1 Fear.”

answers.answer: If Defend reduces Invader Damage to zero, surviving Dahan still counterattack. If the entire Ravage is skipped, they do not counterattack. Presence never counterattacks.
answers.evidence: Ravage: “Surviving Dahan counterattack even when Invader Damage was reduced to zero by Defend, but not when the entire Ravage was skipped. Presence never counterattacks.”

answers.answer: A land with only Explorers still Builds because it has an Invader, and gets a Town unless there are more Towns than Cities. Equal Town and City counts, or more Cities than Towns, also add a Town. More Towns than Cities adds a City. A land with no Invaders adds nothing. Towns are not removed or upgraded.
answers.evidence: Build: “with at least one Invader”; “More Towns than Cities: add a City”; otherwise “including equal counts or only Explorers: add a Town”; “Do not remove or upgrade an existing Town”; empty matching lands do not Build.

answers.answer: A matching land Explores if it contains a Town or City, or is adjacent to a Town, City, or Ocean. Add one Explorer per qualifying land, even if it has multiple sources or already has pieces. Explorers are not Explore sources. If the deck is empty when a card must be drawn, the Spirits lose.
answers.evidence: Explore: add “one Explorer” to each matching land that contains a Town/City or is adjacent to a Town, City, or Ocean; “Existing pieces do not stop Explore; multiple sources still yield just one Explorer. Explorers do not act as sources.” Empty deck rule: “If a card must be drawn and the deck is empty, lose.”

answers.answer: After Explore, discard the old Ravage card, slide Build to Ravage, and move the newly revealed Explore card to Build. A Stage III card showing two terrains affects both, and players may interleave those lands. Ignore Stage II flag/Escalation icons when there is no Adversary.
answers.evidence: Advance cards: “Discard the old Ravage card; slide Build to Ravage and the just-revealed Explore card to Build.” “A Stage III card with two terrains affects both”; “Ignore Stage II flag/Escalation icons without an Adversary.”

answers.answer: With two Spirits the pool is 8 markers. Generating 3 when 7 are already generated exhausts the 8-marker pool and earns one Fear Card; the remaining 2 Fear start toward another card after the pool markers return. The exposed Terror II divider changes the Terror Level immediately. Fear Cards are earned face-down and resolved at the Fear step; if this occurs during the Fear step, resolve in earned order in that same step.
answers.evidence: Fear procedure: “For each Fear, move one marker”; when all “4 per Spirit” have moved, earn the top card face-down, return all markers and continue with leftover Fear. “If earning a card exposes a Terror divider, the new Terror Level applies immediately.” Fear step turns earned stack over and resolves cards in order.

answers.answer: A card earned during the Fear step is appended to the bottom of the resolving stack and resolved in that same Fear step. Subsequent cards use the newly reached Terror Level. “Each player” choices do not require that player’s own Presence or Power Range; players follow the card’s allowed choices, one at a time.
answers.evidence: Fear step: cards earned during this step “append them to the bottom of the resolving stack and resolve them this same step”; “Subsequent cards use any newly reached Terror Level.” Fear effects allow choices “without the player’s own Presence or Power Range.”

answers.answer: Adding one Blight to the already-Blighted land destroys one Presence belonging to each Spirit present there: Spirit A loses one disk and Spirit B loses one disk. Because the land already had Blight, cascade exactly one Blight to one adjacent land chosen by the players. If that adjacent land was already Blighted, adding the cascade Blight destroys one Presence per Spirit there and causes another one-Blight cascade to an adjacent land.
answers.evidence: Blight procedure: “Destroy one Presence from each Spirit with Presence there”; if the land already had Blight, “also add one Blight to one adjacent land chosen by the players”; cascades continue if that destination “was already Blighted.”

answers.answer: Setup Blight comes from the box, never the Blight pool. Blight added after setup comes from the active card or board pool. When a Healthy card pool empties, flip/refill as its reverse directs and add the reverse side’s printed number per Spirit from the box; do not add the setup +1 again. Removing Blight does not restore the Healthy side.
answers.evidence: Setup Blight “comes from the box, never the Blight pool”; later “take Blight added to the island from the active card/board pool.” On flip, “Add the reverse side’s printed number per Spirit from the box; do not add the initial +1 again.” “A Blighted card never becomes Healthy again.”

answers.answer: Elements are checked, not spent, so the same Elements may satisfy multiple Powers and multiple thresholds. An Innate cannot be used twice just because the Spirit has twice the required Elements. All levels of one Innate use the same target; they cannot target different lands. An “Instead” level replaces earlier effects rather than adding to them.
answers.evidence: “Elements are checked, never spent. The same Elements can satisfy multiple Powers and thresholds.” Ordinarily one target land/Spirit, once per turn; “Multiple effects and all innate levels apply to that same target”; cannot use an innate twice by having twice its Elements. “Instead replaces previous effects.”

answers.answer: Yes. If the target is legal, inability to perform one instruction does not prevent using the Power. After starting, the player cannot arbitrarily omit a possible mandatory instruction; instructions are resolved in order, doing as much as possible. The player may forego the entire Power, but receives no Energy refund.
answers.evidence: “Inability to perform one instruction does not prohibit playing or using a Power on an otherwise legal target.” “You may forego the whole Power, but cannot arbitrarily omit a possible mandatory instruction”; forego yields “no Energy refund.”

answers.answer: Choose the Minor or Major deck and draw 4, reshuffling that deck’s discard if needed; keep one in hand and put the other three in that shared deck discard. After gaining a Major, Forget one of your cards permanently, from hand, personal discard, or play, including the Major just gained. A forgotten Minor/Major goes to its shared deck discard; a forgotten Unique goes under the Spirit panel. If forgotten from play, its Elements are immediately lost and its unused activation ends; effects already resolved persist.
answers.evidence: Gain a Power: “draw 4…keep 1 in hand, and discard the rest to that deck’s shared discard.” Major: “Forget one of your cards permanently” from hand, personal discard, or play, including the gained Major. Forgetting from play loses Elements and unused activation; resolved effects persist.

answers.answer: Damage marks Invaders and destroys them when marked Damage reaches their Health; normal Spirit Damage does not harm Dahan or land. Damage from separate normal Powers can accumulate within a turn. Destroy returns pieces regardless of Health and Towns/Cities generate Fear (1/2); Remove returns pieces without destruction Fear. Replace removes a piece and adds another while retaining its marked Damage; the new piece generates no Fear merely for being replaced, but if retained Damage destroys it, ordinary destruction Fear applies.
answers.evidence: Damage section: “Damage from separate normal Powers…can accumulate”; normal Spirit Damage “does not harm Dahan or the land.” Destroy/Fear versus Remove are distinguished; Replace “retaining its marked Damage.”

answers.answer: Increased Power Range does not increase Gather/Push distance. Multiple pieces may come from or go to different adjacent lands. Ordinary movement cannot send pieces into the Ocean. “Up to” allows zero; a numeric instruction without “up to” is mandatory to the extent possible.
answers.evidence: Gather/Push: “Multiple pieces may come from or go to different adjacent lands”; “Increased Power Range does not increase Gather/Push distance”; ordinary movement cannot send pieces “into the Ocean”; “up to” may be zero.

answers.answer: Terror I: no Invaders of any type. Terror II: no Towns or Cities. Terror III: no Cities. At Victory after earning the last Fear Card, win regardless of Invaders. Defeat occurs if any Spirit has no Presence left on the island, the active Blight supply empties and its instructions say to lose, or an Explore card must be drawn but none remains. In the specified Ravage, finish that land’s action tree, including counterattack, before checking outcomes; if both win and loss are met, the Spirits win a sacrifice victory. Do not finish other lands first.
answers.evidence: Scoring/Victory table gives all four Terror conditions. Defeat routes list no Presence, losing Blight supply, and empty Invader deck when a draw is required. Outcome timing says finish current action and triggered actions; check before next land, and if both win and loss apply, “Spirits win a sacrifice victory.”
